data.name: Cataluña
data.summary: Catalonia: wealth tax from EUR 500,000 (0.21%-2.75%, 3.48% above EUR 20m while ITSGF exists); inheritance by children taxed heavily (rebate falls from 60% to 0% as the inheritance grows; about 28% on EUR 10m); gifts 5-9%. Savings income (gains, dividends) is taxed on the national 19-30% scale; the regions cannot change it.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (state rules)
regimes.description: Resident individual taxed on worldwide income and wealth; state rules shown (regional variations in the subnational file).
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence: more than 183 days in Spain in the calendar year, or main centre of economic interests in Spain; presumption if spouse and minor children live in Spain.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains of a resident individual go to the savings base (base del ahorro) and are taxed at 19% to 30%; the top 30% applies to savings income above EUR 300,000 (since 2025). The scale is the same in every common-regime region because the regions cannot change the savings scale.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Savings scale (state + regional half combined, arts. 66 and 76 LIRPF): 19% to EUR 6,000; 21% to 50,000; 23% to 200,000; 27% to 300,000; 30% above. Losses offset savings income within limits; 4-year carry-forward. Gains on the sale of the main home are exempt if reinvested in a new main home or for sellers aged 65+.
capital_gains.regional_differences: No regional difference in the common regime. Navarra and the Basque Country have their own IRPF with a different savings scale (top 28% in Navarra and Bizkaia, see the subnational file).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Exit tax (art. 95 bis LIRPF): a resident for at least 10 of the last 15 years who leaves Spain is taxed on the unrealised gain on shares if their market value exceeds EUR 4m, or EUR 1m with a stake above 25%; deferral is available on moves within the EU/EEA. Funds (IIC) can be switched without tax (traspasos). Selling Spanish property also triggers the municipal IIVTNU.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Top marginal rate of the combined savings scale (30% above EUR 300,000) for a large gain; no holding period matters. Real estate gains of individuals are savings income too (municipal IIVTNU on Spanish land comes on top and is not included).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains on securities remain savings income for a private investor regardless of volume; only an organised business activity (e.g. a dealer with staff and premises) would move income to the general base (state+regional up to about 45-54%).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None. Short- and long-term gains are taxed alike; 2-month/1-year wash-sale rules defer losses on repurchased securities.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains with a credit for foreign tax (art. 80 LIRPF). Foreign assets above EUR 50,000 per category must be reported on Modelo 720.

dividends.summary: Dividends are savings income taxed at 19% to 30% (30% above EUR 300,000 of savings income), domestic and foreign alike. Foreign withholding tax is credited up to the Spanish tax on that income.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: No dividend exemption for individuals (the former EUR 1,500 exemption was abolished in 2015).
dividends.regional_differences: None in the common regime; Navarra and the Basque Country have their own scales (see subnational file).

dividends.rate_basis: Top marginal rate of the savings scale (art. 66/76 LIRPF) for a large portfolio; credit for foreign WHT limited to the treaty rate and to the Spanish tax on that income (art. 80 LIRPF).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 19% domestic WHT on dividends to non-residents; 0% to qualifying EU parents (5% for 1 year); treaty rates usually 0-15%.
dividends.treaty_network: About 90-plus treaties in force (PwC lists 92 entries), including the US (15% portfolio dividends) and all EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: A Spanish S.L. holding is scored as the regime 'holding_sl'. A company holding a diversified listed portfolio pays 25% on dividends (net of the foreign withholding credited, art. 31 LIS) and on gains, because the 95% exemption of art. 21 LIS needs a stake of at least 5% held one year (the EUR 20 million alternative was removed from 2021); it is an entidad patrimonial (art. 5.2 LIS), so it cannot use the reduced rates and its shares get no wealth-tax business exemption; distributions are then taxed again at up to 30%. A SICAV's 1% rate is out of reach for a single family (100 shareholders, art. 9.4 Ley 35/2003, referred to by art. 29.4 LIS). A private foundation cannot be used: Spanish foundations must serve general-interest purposes and may not be set up mainly to benefit the founder or relatives to the fourth degree (arts. 2 and 3 Ley 50/2002). Spain has no domestic trust law; a foreign trust is treated as transparent, its assets staying with the settlor (not opened).

wealth_tax.summary: Catalonia: IP payable with a EUR 500,000 allowance and a regional scale 0.21%-2.75%, plus a 3.48% band above EUR 20m base while the ITSGF exists (Decreto-ley 10/2024). The ITSGF tops up only where it exceeds IP (roughly above EUR 17.5m of base per person). Scored for the reference couple (each spouse taxed separately, with the EUR 500,000 allowance and EUR 300,000 main-home exemption), net wealth including the home: EUR 10m: EUR 108,877; EUR 20m: EUR 319,734; EUR 35m: EUR 715,928 before the joint IRPF limit.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Allowance EUR 500,000 per person; main home EUR 300,000 per person (state). Scale art. 621-2 and DT 1ª Libro sexto Código tributario (D.Leg. 1/2024). Allowance and scale are fixed by law and not indexed.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Bonuses only for protected disability assets (99%) and managed forests (95%).

components.name: IP Cataluña + ITSGF top-up, married couple owning 50/50
components.notes: Brackets encode the combined burden max(regional IP, ITSGF) computed from the official scales. Written for the reference couple owning the wealth 50/50 and taxed separately: per person the allowance is 500,000 (art. 621-1 Libro sexto Código tributario) plus 300,000 for the main home (art. 4.Nueve LIP), so 1,600,000 for the couple, and every bracket limit is doubled (single limits 167,129.45 ... 10,695,996.06 from art. 621-2; the ITSGF takes over above 17,046,647.47 of base). The engine passes net wealth including the home, so the home exemption is folded into the allowance. The joint IRPF limit (art. 31 LIP: IRPF + IP at most 60% of the IRPF base, IP cut by at most 80%) is ignored.

income_cap.notes: Art. 31 Ley 19/1991 (and art. 3.Doce Ley 38/2022 for the ITSGF): the IRPF cuota on the general and savings bases plus wealth tax may not exceed 60% of the IRPF taxable base, leaving out gains on assets held over a year; the wealth tax is cut to fit, by at most 80%. Applied per spouse; with a 50/50 split the couple's figures are twice one spouse's.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax (IBI, roughly 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value) and the municipal land-value gain tax on sales (IIVTNU) are ordinary local taxes and are not modelled as wealth tax.

inheritance.summary: Catalonia: children 21+ get EUR 100,000 reduction, scale 7%-32%, and a rebate that falls from 60% (first EUR 100,000 of base) to 0% (above EUR 3m) as a weighted average; about 19.6% of a EUR 9m estate split between three children (EUR 586,437 each), 20.7% of EUR 10m, and about 28% for a single heir inheriting EUR 10m.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Group II reduction EUR 100,000 per child (art. 631-2); scale 7/11/17/24/32% (art. 633-1); multipliers 1.0-1.2 (1.1 from EUR 500,000 of pre-existing wealth); rebate table art. 633-4.2.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Brackets are a piecewise-linear fit of tax = scale x (1 - weighted-average rebate), exact at the rebate band edges, multiplier 1.0. Using family-business or other optional reductions forfeits the rebate.

inheritance.spouse_note: Spouse gets EUR 100,000 reduction, then the 7%-32% scale, and a 99% bonificación of the tax reserved for the spouse (art. 633-4.1 Libro sexto Código tributario, D.Leg. 1/2024), with no base cap: about 0.3%-0.4% of a large estate, unlike children whose rebate falls to 0%. inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts to children: special scale 5% to EUR 200,000, 7% to EUR 600,000, 9% above, if in a public deed (Libro sexto art. 633-2); about 8.8% on a EUR 10m gift. No gift rebate.
inheritance.business_relief: State 95% reduction for qualifying family businesses, raised to 99% in many regions, with residence/holding conditions; not for listed portfolios.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Resident heirs are taxed on worldwide acquisitions, with credit for foreign inheritance tax.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Regional rules apply to inheritances when the deceased spent most days of the last 5 years in this region (art. 28 Ley 22/2009) and to gifts of movable assets when the donee did; otherwise state or another region's rules apply. Non-resident heirs may also use them (DA 2ª Ley 29/1987).

regimes.name: Special regime for inbound workers (art. 93 LIRPF, 'Beckham law')
regimes.description: For 6 tax years (year of arrival + 5) the person is taxed like a non-resident: foreign-source dividends, interest and capital gains are not taxed; Spanish-source savings income is taxed at 19-30%; employment income at 24% up to EUR 600,000 and 47% above. Wealth tax only on Spanish assets.
regimes.eligibility: Not Spanish tax resident in the previous 5 years, and moving because of: a Spanish employment contract (including remote work for a foreign employer with the international telework visa), becoming director of a company (if it is a holding/patrimonial company, without a stake of 25% or more), a certified entrepreneurial activity, or highly qualified work for start-ups/R&D. No Spanish permanent establishment. Election within 6 months of starting work. Spouse and children under 25 can join if their combined base is below the main taxpayer's. A pure investor with no Spanish job or directorship does not qualify.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign capital gains are not taxed in Spain during the regime; gains on Spanish assets are taxed at 19% to 30%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Spanish-source savings income scale 19%/21%/23%/27%/30% (30% above EUR 300,000; art. 93.2.e).2º LIRPF as amended by DF 7.3 Ley 7/2024, effective 1 January 2025).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Employment income is taxed worldwide. Top rate on Spanish-source savings income: the BOE consolidated text of art. 93.2.e).2º LIRPF shows the scale 19% (to EUR 6,000), 21% (to 50,000), 23% (to 200,000), 27% (to 300,000) and 30% above, as amended by disposición final 7.3 of Ley 7/2024 (BOE-A-2024-26694) with effect from 1 January 2025; PwC's page (reviewed June 2026) still shows the pre-2025 28%, which is out of date. After the regime ends, the person is a normal resident; exit tax counts years of residence including the regime years.

regimes.name: Family holding company (S.L., sociedad patrimonial) taxed at 25%
regimes.description: The family holds its listed shares through a Spanish S.L. (corporate income tax 25%, art. 29.1 LIS). A company whose assets are mostly securities is an 'entidad patrimonial' (art. 5.2 LIS): it gets no reduced CIT rate (art. 29.1 LIS) and its shares get no wealth-tax or inheritance-tax business exemption (art. 4.Ocho.Dos.a LIP). The 95% participation exemption (art. 21 LIS) needs a stake of at least 5% held for a year, which a diversified listed portfolio never reaches (the old EUR 20 million cost alternative was removed from 1 January 2021 by art. 65 Ley 11/2020), so dividends and gains are taxed at 25%; foreign withholding on dividends is credited (art. 31 LIS). Distributions to the family are dividends in the savings base, taxed at up to 30% (arts. 25, 66, 76 LIRPF). Wealth tax and inheritance tax fall on the family's shares as for direct holding, so the regional rules apply.
regimes.eligibility: Any Spanish tax resident can form an S.L. (minimum share capital EUR 1). Contributing existing shares is a disposal taxed in the contributor's IRPF (savings scale), so it suits cash or newly bought assets.
regimes.duration_note: A holding company has no statutory time limit; it lasts as long as the family keeps it and stays resident, subject to changes in the law.

structure.entity: Sociedad de responsabilidad limitada (S.L.) family holding company (entidad patrimonial)
structure.payout_notes: Dividends to resident individuals are capital income from equity (art. 25.1.a LIRPF) in the savings base, taxed on the 19% to 30% scale (arts. 66 and 76 LIRPF; 27% from EUR 200,000 and 30% above EUR 300,000 of savings income per person). The 30% top rate is used, as for direct holding; on a payout of about EUR 515,000 gross shared by two spouses the average is lower for now but thresholds are fixed in euros, so spending that grows with prices reaches the 30% band. Spanish withholding on the payout (19%) is credited against the personal tax. No allowance or exemption for dividends.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Entidad patrimonial (art. 5.2 LIS): more than half of the assets are securities, so the company carries on no economic activity. Consequences: no reduced CIT rates (art. 29.1 LIS, last paragraph); the 95% exemption of art. 21 LIS needs a stake of at least 5% held a year (art. 21.1.a), and for foreign investees tax of at least 10% nominal (art. 21.1.b); the family's shares do not qualify for the wealth-tax exemption of art. 4.Ocho.Dos.a LIP (entity must not mainly manage a securities or property portfolio) nor, because that exemption is a condition, for the 95% inheritance-tax reduction of art. 20.2.c LISD. The 1% SICAV rate (art. 29.4 LIS) needs the minimum number of shareholders of art. 9.4 Ley 35/2003 (100), out of reach for one family. The company must keep real books and file annual accounts; Spain's general anti-abuse rule (art. 15 Ley General Tributaria) can recharacterise arrangements without a valid business purpose (not opened). Statutory audit is assumed not required: the company has no staff and low turnover (art. 263 Ley de Sociedades de Capital, not opened). Gains on shares held by the company are taxed on realisation at 25% with no holding-period relief.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: On liquidation the company is taxed at 25% on latent gains, then the shareholders are taxed in the savings base on the liquidation proceeds above the cost of their shares (arts. 25 and 33 LIRPF). On death the heirs' shares are valued by the inheritance tax and the heirs' acquisition value is stepped up (death transfers produce no gain, art. 33.3.b LIRPF), but the company keeps its own historic cost for the portfolio, so the latent gain inside the company is still taxed at 25% when realised.

capital_gains.important_exceptions: Funds and ETFs also 25% at realisation. A stake of at least 5% in an investee would be 95% exempt (effective 1.25%), but is not a portfolio case.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by the S.L. are taxed at 25% (art. 29.1 LIS) because the holdings are under 5% (art. 21.1.a LIS). Foreign withholding tax is credited up to the lesser of the foreign tax paid and the Spanish tax on that income (art. 31 LIS), so a 15% treaty withholding leaves a net 10% Spanish cost on foreign dividends. Spanish dividends suffer a 19% withholding, which is credited against the 25%, so the cost is 25% in all.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: 95% exemption only for stakes of at least 5% held a year (and, for foreign investees, tax of at least 10% nominal there).

income.name: Spain

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax is the sum of a state and a regional scale. For Madrid the combined marginal rates on the general base run 18% to 45% (43% from EUR 60,000, 45% above EUR 300,000). Employee social security is 6.5% (capped at the maximum monthly base EUR 5,101.20, EUR 61,214.40 a year); autonomos pay 31.5% on a chosen base within the same maximum. The recorded personal allowance is the EUR 5,550 personal minimum; strictly it is taxed at the lowest rates rather than deducted, and employees also get a EUR 2,000 expenses deduction (not modelled).

employment_deduction.note: 'Other expenses' deduction for employment income of EUR 2,000 a year (the extra reduction below EUR 19,747.50 is not modelled).

source.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Spain, deductions

income_tax.self_employed_notes: Autonomos (RETA) pay 31.5% in 2026 (common contingencies 28.30%, professional 1.30%, cessation 0.90%, training 0.10%, MEI 0.90%; Seguridad Social page) on a monthly base they choose within the band set by their net monthly income (12 general brackets; maximum base EUR 5,101.20, so at most EUR 19,283 a year in contributions). For net income of about EUR 4,500 a month (EUR 54k) bracket 11 applies: base EUR 1,732.03 to 5,101.20, i.e. EUR 545.59 to 1,606.88 a month, EUR 6,547 to 19,283 a year (12% to 36% of EUR 54k). The 31.5% flat rate used in the model is therefore a ceiling for incomes below the cap. Business income is reduced by a flat EUR 2,000 deduction; health premiums are deductible up to EUR 500 per person. Employees above the maximum base also pay a solidarity contribution (1.15% to 1.46% on the excess, 16.61% of it borne by the employee).
income_tax.local_tax_note: Madrid autonomous-community scale (8.5% to 20.5%; thresholds EUR 13,362 / 19,005 / 35,426 / 57,320, Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 as deflated by Ley 13/2023, per Guia Fiscal and Taxdown) is combined with the state scale (9.5% to 24.5%) in the brackets. Other regions differ (Catalonia is higher). Both Madrid tables are tax-advice sites that agree with each other; the BOCM was not opened.

regimes.name: International teleworker visa (digital nomad visa)
regimes.description: Residence visa for non-EU remote workers (Ley 14/2013 art. 74 as amended by the Startups Law 28/2022). Requires funds of at least 200% of the monthly minimum wage (2026 SMI EUR 1,221 x 14 = EUR 17,094 a year, so EUR 34,188 a year; BOE RD 126/2026 and the New York consulate page), a degree or 3 years of experience, 3 months of relationship with the foreign employer or clients, and for the self-employed at most 20% of activity for Spanish clients. Tax treatment is not changed by the visa: holders who become resident pay normal IRPF, but employees (not self-employed) holding the visa may opt for the Beckham regime (esp_beckham_teleworker).
regimes.duration_note: Visa valid 1 year from a consulate; from inside Spain a permit of up to 3 years, renewable in 2-year steps to a maximum of 5 years.

sources.title: Visado de teletrabajo (Spanish consulate in New York)

open_questions: The 200%-of-SMI test is stated by the consulate; the EUR 34,188 a year (EUR 2,849 a month over 12) is our arithmetic from the BOE SMI of EUR 1,221 x 14. Remote Work Europe quotes the same figure.
Employees need a social security registration or an A1 certificate; autonomos register in RETA.
Duration: consulate page says visa 1 year, permit up to 3 years from inside Spain; the 5-year maximum with renewals rests on Remote Work Europe.

regimes.name: Special regime for displaced workers (Beckham law) - employee with a Spanish contract
regimes.description: Art. 93 LIRPF (Ley 35/2006, consolidated BOE text): optional taxation under the non-resident (IRNR) rules while staying IRPF-resident: 24% flat on Spanish-source work income up to EUR 600,000 and 47% above; foreign-source income is outside Spanish tax (savings income at 19-30%). Applies for the arrival year plus five years. Conditions: not Spanish resident in the previous five tax years and a move because of an employment contract in Spain (or a posting letter), appointment as company director, entrepreneurial activity certified under art. 70 Ley 14/2013, or work as a highly qualified professional for start-ups/R&D with over 40% of income from it. Application within six months of starting work (Modelo 149). Remote employees of foreign firms with the teleworker visa are modelled separately (esp_beckham_teleworker).
regimes.duration_note: Arrival year plus the five following tax years.

sources.title: Ley 35/2006 del IRPF, art. 93 (consolidated text)
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Spain, other issues (special expatriate regime)

open_questions: Self-employed professionals qualify only through the entrepreneur-activity (art. 70 Ley 14/2013) or highly-qualified start-up/R&D routes (art. 93.1.b.3-4), which need certification; not modelled as a general self-employment route.

regimes.name: Beckham law for teleworker-visa employees of foreign companies
regimes.description: Since the Startups Law (Ley 28/2022) art. 93.1.b.1 LIRPF says the displacement condition is met when the work is done remotely using exclusively IT/telecoms systems, and 'in particular' for employees (trabajadores por cuenta ajena) holding the international teleworker visa of Ley 14/2013. They can opt for the IRNR-style regime: 24% flat on their work income up to EUR 600,000 (47% above); art. 93.2.b deems all work income earned during the regime to be Spanish-source, so pay for work done in Spain is covered. The statute names employees only: a self-employed teleworker visa holder is not named (applies_to is therefore employment only). Needs no prior Spanish residence in five years and the visa's own conditions (funds of EUR 34,188 a year).
regimes.duration_note: Regime lasts the arrival year plus five years (6 tax years); the teleworker permit itself runs to 5 years with renewals, so 5 is used.

open_questions: Self-employed visa holders: art. 93.1.b.1 names 'trabajadores por cuenta ajena' only and the work-from-abroad wording refers to 'actividad laboral'; the self-employed are not covered unless they meet the entrepreneur or start-up routes. No tax-authority (DGT) ruling was opened.

income.residence_routes: EU citizens live and work freely and register as residents. US and other non-EU remote workers can use the international teleworker visa (200% of the minimum wage, at most 20% Spanish clients for the self-employed, degree or 3 years of experience), valid up to five years with renewals. Skilled employees from outside the EU need a work-residence authorisation sponsored by a Spanish employer, which is not researched here; the Beckham regime applies to either group once resident.

succession.name: Spain
succession.summary: Under the common law, children are guaranteed two thirds of the estate and a will cannot remove it. A foreign national resident can choose their national law under the EU Succession Regulation. Foral regions differ, and Spain has no trust law and no private family foundation.
succession.reserved_share: Common Civil Code: children and descendants 2/3 (1/3 strict legitima, 1/3 free to distribute among them, art. 806-808); ascendants 1/2 or 1/3 if there is a spouse (art. 809) when there are no descendants; the spouse gets a usufruct (art. 834 ff.). Foral law differs: Catalonia 1/4 as a money claim; Navarre only a symbolic share; the Basque Country (Ley 5/2015) a collective 1/3; Aragon a collective 1/2 (regional figures from secondary guides).
succession.foreign_law_note: Reg. 650/2012 art. 22 allows a choice of nationality law for the whole estate, which removes the legitima. For a foreigner, regional law follows habitual residence (art. 36), so the foral rules apply to foreigners living in a foral region.
succession.trust_note: Spain has no trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. The HCCH status table lists no signature or ratification for this state; the Convention is not in force here. Foreign trusts are not specifically regulated and are dealt with case by case for tax. Foundations (Ley 50/2002) must serve general-interest purposes and cannot mainly benefit the founder or family, so a private family foundation is not available.
open_questions: Regional legitima figures come from secondary guides and were not checked against the foral statutes.
Spanish tax treatment of foreign trusts was not researched.
Art. numbers in Ley 50/2002 on the ban on family benefit were not verified.

assumptions: The family is an EU-citizen couple with no Spanish job or business, owning the wealth 50/50 and taxed separately (Spanish wealth tax and IRPF are individual taxes). The tax files encode the couple by doubling each spouse's allowance and bracket limits, which is exact for an equal split.

The Beckham regime (art. 93 LIRPF) needs a Spanish employment contract, a directorship or a qualifying entrepreneurial activity, so this family cannot use it and it has no path (the tax file marks it requires_qualifying_activity).

Savings income (dividends, gains, payouts) is taxed at the top rate of 30% (arts. 66 and 76 LIRPF), assuming both spouses are above EUR 300,000 of savings income. A smaller income would pay 19% to 27% on the lower slices, so the scores are slightly high for modest portfolios.

Each death passes the whole estate (portfolio and home) to the three children, who are adults (21 or over) with pre-existing wealth within the lowest coefficient band of the inheritance tax (coefficient 1.0).

Declarations are made on time, in a notarial deed where required, so regional rebates apply. Lifetime gifts to children are not modelled; they are taxed under a different regional scale (see the tax file).

The S.L. holding is funded with cash or newly bought assets (contributing existing shares is a taxable disposal for the contributor) and keeps its books at fair value, so the inherited shares are valued at about the portfolio's value; a deferred-tax liability on unrealised gains could lower the theoretical value used for wealth and inheritance tax, which is not assumed.

Catalonia's wealth tax scale has a 3.48% band above EUR 20m of base per person while the ITSGF exists (Decreto-ley 10/2024), and the ITSGF (3.5%) takes over from the IP above about EUR 17.05m of base per person; the tax file encodes the larger of the two.

Catalonia is the heavier of the two cases for inheritance: the child's rebate is a weighted average that is 60% on the first EUR 100,000 of base and falls to 0% marginal above EUR 3m. Lifetime gifts to children in a notarial deed pay only 5% to 9% (art. 633-2), so the real family might gift in life; the engine does not model gifts, which makes Catalonia look worse than it need be.

A private foundation is not a path: Spanish foundations must pursue general-interest purposes and may not be formed mainly to benefit the founder or relatives to the fourth degree (arts. 2 and 3 Ley 50/2002); Catalan foundations fall under Libro tercer of the Catalan Civil Code, which was not opened. A family trust has no basis in Spanish law and is treated as transparent (the assets stay taxed as the settlor's), so it changes nothing. The SICAV's 1% rate needs 100 shareholders (art. 29.4 LIS). The ETVE regime does not fit a diversified listed portfolio.

Checks assume a main home worth at least EUR 300,000 per spouse: its exemption (art. 4.Nueve LIP) is folded into the wealth-tax allowance, as for the family's EUR 5M home. The joint limit is applied at top marginal rates (the real family's dividends are about EUR 600,000); on small incomes the progressive IRPF scale would give a slightly different cut.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the inheritance-tax coefficient that depends on the heir's pre-existing wealth (art. 22 Ley 29/1987; Catalonia art. 633-3 Libro sexto Código tributario: 1.10 above EUR 500,000, 1.15 above EUR 2,000,000, 1.20 above EUR 4,000,000). A child who already holds over EUR 500,000 pays 10% to 20% more on the cuota, before the rebate, and a child enriched by the first death will usually do so at the second; the engine has no per-heir wealth, so it applies the coefficient of 1.0, a floor.

Needs an engine change: lifetime gifts. A notarial gift to a child is taxed at 5% to EUR 200,000, 7% to EUR 600,000 and 9% above (art. 633-2 Libro sexto Código tributario), far below the 20% to 30% on a large inheritance (Madrid: 99% bonificación for gifts too). The engine taxes transfers only at the two deaths, so a family that gifts in life is not shown.
Catalonia's own foundation law (Libro tercer del Código civil de Cataluña) was not opened; the general-interest requirement for foundations is cited from the state law, Ley 50/2002.

The citations to Ley 22/2009 art. 28, art. 10.3 LIS, art. 20.2.c Ley 29/1987 and art. 22 Ley 29/1987 were not opened as text; the Catalan wealth and inheritance scales, reductions, coefficients and rebate tables were read in the Ministerio de Hacienda document 'Medidas 2026'.

ITSGF with a holding S.L.: whether the 80% maximum reduction of the joint limit (art. 3.Doce Ley 38/2022) is applied before or after deducting the regional wealth tax paid (art. 3.Quince) is not settled by any AEAT guidance found (modelo 718 instructions unavailable); applied after, the S.L. path's wealth tax would be about 20% higher. An independent check computed EUR 73,450 / 75,449 for the two S.L. annual checks under that reading.
Catalan bonificación: art. 633-4.5 Codi tributari rounds the weighted average to two decimals (28.92%), about EUR 27 per child less than the unrounded rate in the check.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence, Cataluña)
paths.note: Dividends and gains go to the savings base at 19% to 30% (30% above EUR 300,000 per person), the foreign withholding being credited (art. 80 LIRPF). Catalonia levies its own wealth tax: EUR 500,000 allowance per person and a scale of 0.21% to 2.75% (3.48% above EUR 20m while the ITSGF exists), so a EUR 10m couple pays about EUR 109,000 a year before the joint IRPF limit. Children inheriting pay the Catalan scale (7% to 32%) with a rebate that falls from 60% to 0% as the inheritance grows, so a large inheritance is taxed heavily.

paths.name: Family holding company (S.L.) taxed at 25%
paths.regime: Family holding company (S.L., sociedad patrimonial) taxed at 25%
paths.note: An S.L. owns the portfolio and pays 25% corporate tax on dividends (foreign withholding credited, so 10% net on foreign dividends) and on gains; the 95% participation exemption (art. 21 LIS) needs a stake of at least 5%, which a diversified portfolio lacks. The family's payouts are dividends taxed at up to 30%. As a securities-holding company (entidad patrimonial, art. 5.2 LIS) its shares get no wealth-tax or inheritance-tax business relief (and in Catalonia the 95% reduction forfeits the rebate anyway), so the Catalan wealth and inheritance tax apply as for direct holding. Costs about EUR 3,300 a year.

immigration.name: Spain
immigration.summary: EU citizens only register. Non-EU citizens (US and others) can use the non-lucrative visa (EUR 28,800 a year of passive income, no work), the digital nomad visa (about EUR 34,000 a year of foreign remote income), or an entrepreneur or work permit. The golden visa ended on 3 April 2025.
immigration.naturalisation: General rule: 10 years of legal, continuous residence immediately before applying, a Spanish A2 language certificate (DELE) and the CCSE civics test; shorter periods for refugees (5 years) and, per general knowledge not re-sourced, 2 years for Ibero-American nationals, Andorra, Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal and Sephardic descendants.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Applicants normally must renounce their previous nationality, except nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea and Portugal (Civil Code art. 23; from general knowledge, not re-sourced).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement (certificado de registro)
routes.summary: EU citizens enter freely and register in Spain after 3 months.
routes.requirements: Valid ID or passport. Beyond 3 months register as a worker, self-employed person, student or economically inactive person with sufficient resources and health cover. Permanent right of residence after 5 years of continuous legal residence (Directive 2004/38).
routes.physical_presence: No fixed minimum; continuity of residence counts
routes.family: Spouse, partner and dependants have derived rights.
routes.tax_note: Registration does not decide tax residence; the 183-day test and centre of economic interests do.

routes.name: Non-lucrative residence visa
routes.summary: Residence for people who live on savings or passive income and do not work in Spain. Income of 400% of IPREM, EUR 28,800 a year in 2026.
routes.requirements: Income of 400% of the monthly IPREM (IPREM EUR 600 a month in 2026), i.e. EUR 2,400 a month or EUR 28,800 a year for the main applicant, plus 100% of IPREM (EUR 7,200 a year) per family member. Private health insurance with no co-pay; clean record. No work allowed in Spain. Consulates assess case by case.
routes.family: Each family member adds EUR 7,200 a year to the income test.
routes.tax_note: Living in Spain more than 183 days makes you tax resident on worldwide income; Beckham regime is not available on this visa.

routes.name: Digital nomad visa (teleworker, Ley 28/2022)
routes.summary: For remote workers employed by or serving clients outside Spain; income of EUR 2,849 a month (about EUR 34,188 a year) in 2026 per one source.
routes.requirements: Income of at least 200% of the minimum wage as stated by the source: EUR 2,849 a month for a single applicant in 2026 (the source's arithmetic does not reconcile with the EUR 1,221 SMI, so verify); dependants add 75% of SMI for the first and 25% for each further. At least 80% of income from outside Spain. Consulate application gives 1 year, in-Spain application 3 years; renewals in 2-year steps up to 5 years.
routes.fees_note: Application fee EUR 80 to 100 plus about EUR 15 to 20 for the TIE card, per Remote Work Europe; upper bound used.
routes.physical_presence: At least 6 months a year to renew; absences over 6 consecutive months can block renewal
routes.family: Dependants can be added with higher income.
routes.tax_note: Holders may elect the Beckham regime (24% on Spanish-source income up to EUR 600,000, 6 years); self-employed nomads generally do not qualify, per source.

routes.requirements: Business plan assessed by ENISA and the Spanish authorities; no statutory investment figure sourced here. Opens access to the Beckham regime.
